A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPEED and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables and complete appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original concept-erasure experiments, benchmark comparisons, ablations and adversarial evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds a human evaluation of instance-erasure efficacy in Appendix D.1, Table 5.

M1.justification: The null-space editing procedure, IPF, DPA, IEC, objectives and closed-form updates are retained. The cross-model and adversarial-training adaptations already appeared in v2.

E1.justification: Concepts, datasets, attack scenarios and cross-model applications remain unchanged. The human study assesses existing Snoopy, Mickey and Spongebob erasure outputs without broadening the represented concept or input coverage.

E2.justification: Baseline membership is unchanged in corresponding main-text and appendix comparisons. The added human study reuses RECE, which was already compared against SPEED on these instance concepts.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a human-evaluation protocol: 50 generated images per method as stated, 30 Mechanical Turk participants, and binary judgments of whether the target concept was erased. Existing generation settings, benchmark protocols and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: The new human study provides a focused supplementary check that moderate CLIP scores still correspond to successful visual erasure. Existing component, parameter and hyperparameter ablations and adversarial-robustness analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The human study adds percentages and averages without uncertainty analysis; its participant count is an evaluation sample size.

E6.justification: V4 Table 5 adds human-rated erasure percentages for three concepts, averaging 98.47% for SPEED and 98.76% for RECE. Existing benchmark scores, runtimes, ablation values and qualitative examples are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and Appendix B assumptions, lower-bound proof and closed-form derivations remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same mathematical preliminaries.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable, precise and efficient erasure, superior preservation, and erasing 100 concepts in five seconds. The human study supplies additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 more explicitly conditions the over-erasure argument on further CLIP-score reductions after successful erasure. Appendix D.1 interprets the human results as supporting adequate erasure comparable to RECE; the principal mechanism explanations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 Table 2 specifies that runtimes were measured on one A100 GPU; v4 removes this disclosure without giving replacement hardware information. Existing erasure configurations, hyperparameters and code/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations including Yan et al. (2024), Wu et al. (2025a,b), Wang et al. (2024c), Li et al. (2025), and Mechanical Turk. The positioning relative to training-based, editing-based and null-space methods remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 makes limited prose and terminology edits, updates authorship, affiliations, headers and citation formatting, and adds an LLM Usage Statement before the limitations. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V4 adds human-study Table 5, changes Table 1's pink shading to identify target concepts, and relocates existing appendix figures and tables. Subsequent tables are renumbered, while existing visual examples and plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The added human study modestly strengthens v2's example-based argument that effective erasure can coexist with moderate CLIP scores. Its narrow coverage and missing uncertainty analysis limit the gain. Removal of the A100 disclosure and unreconciled ethics wording about human subjects are reporting regressions, but the direct human validation provides a small net improvement.
